बधिर: Badhira m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 16, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
बलहेड: Balaheḍa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those who were offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 8, 7, 9.
बलाह: Balāha m.: Name of Kṛṣṇa's horse. [See Balāhaka2]
बलाहक: Balāhaka1 m.: A mythical serpent. One of the serpents who, without feeling fatigue (विगतक्लम), wait upon Varuṇa in his सभा; described as marked with banner (पताकिन्), round spots (मण्डलिन्), and hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 9, 10, 11.

Balāhaka2, Balāha m.: Name of one of the four horses yoked to Kṛṣṇa's chariot. They all were of excellent Kamboja-breed (परमकाम्बोज) 10. 13. 1; decorated with gold strings (हेममालिन् 10. 13. 1) and gold-harness (हेमभाण्डविभूषित 7. 122. 45); endowed with all excellences (सर्वसंपद्-) 5. 81. 19; very swift (महावेग) and could go where they desired (कामग) 7. 122. 45; 10. 13. 9; when they sped along they appeared to swallow the sky (ते ग्रसन्त इवाकाशं वेगवन्तो महाबलाः) 12. 53. 22-23; all the four horses specially marked for their speed, hence Uttara compared his right side-horse with Balāhaka and thought him to be speedier than Balāhaka 4. 40. 21; Balāhaka was one of the two side-horses (पार्ष्णिवाह), he being on the right side 4. 40. 21; 10. 13. 2; Balāhaka mentioned among the four horses yoked to Kṛṣṇa's chariot when it was got ready for various occasions—for Kṛṣṇa when he proceeded to Hāstinapura on his peace mission 5. 81. 19; for Kṛṣṇa's likely intervention in war to kill Karṇa, Droṇa and the rest and to enable Arjuna kill Jayadratha within the stipulated time 7. 56. 35, 25-37; for the use by Sātyaki when he lost his chariot while fighting with Karṇa 7. 122. 45; for Kṛṣṇa when he followed Bhīma who had left in pursuit of Aśvatthāman 10. 13. 1-2; for Kṛṣṇa when he started to visit Bhīṣma lying on his bed of arrows at Kurukṣetra 12. 53. 21 (here short form Balāha).
बाहुक: Bāhuka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Kauravya, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 12, 1, 3.

Bāhuka m. (pl.): Name of a people. They brought for the Rājasūya tribute in the form of large quantities of gold and silver, but were stopped at the gate (बाहुकान् … । … द्वारि वारीतान्॑बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्मै हिरण्यं रजतं बहु ॥ ) 2. 47. 15-Jo.
बाह्यकर्ण: Bāhyakarṇa m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 9, 2.
बाह्यकुण्ड: Bāhyakuṇḍa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 10, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
बिल्वपत्र: Bilvapatra m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 14, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
बिल्वपाण्डुक: Bilvapāṇḍuka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 12, 2.
बार्हस्पत्य: Bārhaspatya m.: A particular arrange-ment of the army (व्यूह) originating with Bṛhaspati. Described as chief of the व्यूहस् (व्यूहराज) 8. 31. 25, great व्यूह (महा-व्यूह) that caused fear to the enemies 8. 31. 26, 29; it consisted of ‘wings’ (पक्ष) and ‘extensions or extremities of wings’ (प्रपक्ष) 8. 31. 6, 29; it was used by Karṇa on the seventeenth day of the war to attack the Parānīkabhid Vyūha of the Pāṇḍavas 8. 31. 5, 1; its ‘right wing’ (दक्षिण पक्ष) was constituted by Kṛpa, the Magadha warriors (मगधश् च (?) 8. 31. 11, v. l. मागधास् च), and Kṛtavarman; the wing was further extended (प्रपक्ष) by stationing there Śakuni and Ulūka, who were guarded by horsemen from Gandhāra country (सादिभिः … गान्धारिभिः 8. 31. 12-13) and invincible warriors from highlands (पार्वतीयैश् च दुर्जयैः 8. 31. 13); on the ‘left side’ (वाम पार्श्व) stood the Saṃ-śaptakas with thirty-four thousand chariot-fighters, who would not leave the battle, together with the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; the left wing was further extended (प्रपक्ष) by ordering the Kāmbojas, the Śakas and the Yavanas to be there; they were there with chariots and horse-men, and foot-soldiers; in the middle of the front of the army stood Karṇa himself to guard it; he was offered protection by his sons; he looked suitable as the leader of the व्यूह; the rear (पृष्ठतः) of the army was taken care of by Duḥ-śāsana, seated on a huge elephant (महा-द्विपस्कन्धगतः 8. 31. 19) and surrounded by different armies; he was followed by Duryodhana with his brothers on horse-backs, and the Madras and the Kekayas to protect him; Aśvatthāman, the Kuru heroes, and elephants mounted by the Mlecchas were behind the army of the chariot-fighters (अन्व-युस् तद् रथानीकम्); they were assisted by horse-men (सादिभिश् चास्थिताः); many thousands of brave warriors, who would not show their backs, armed with पट्टिश and swords, acted as foot-guards of elephants and of foot-soldiers (?) (तेषां पदातिनागानां पादरक्षाः सहस्रशः 8. 31. 24); the Bārhaspatya vyūha shone like the army of the gods or of the Asuras 8. 31. 11-25.

Bārhaspatya nt.: Name of a शास्त्र in the form of an abridgement made by Bṛhas-pati 12. 59. 90. The original Nītiśāstra composed by Lokapitāmaha (Brahmadeva) was succes-sively abridged by Śiva, Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Kāvya; Bṛhaspati apparently received the abridged form known as Bāhudantaka from Indra; he then further abridged it to three thousand अध्यायस्; (this was further abridged by Kāvya, the teacher of the Yoga (योगाचार्य) into one thousand अध्यायस्-the name of this last abridgement not given 12. 59. 91). [See Paitāmahaśāstra, Bāhu-dantaka, Vaiśālākṣa].
बाहुकण्टक: Bāhukaṇṭaka nt.: Name of a particular manœuvre employed in a wrestling match. Karṇa employed it to split the joint in Jarāsandha's body while wrestling with him (but did not kill him) (बाहुभिः समसञ्-जेताम् उभाव् अपि बलान्वितौ ॥ बाहुकण्टक-युद्धेन तस्य कर्णो ऽथ युध्यतः बिभेद सन्धिं देहस्य) 12. 5. 3-4 [बाहु-कण्टकं (बहु-कण्टकं ?) केतकपत्रम् तद्वद् यत्र बलिना दुर्बलस्य शरीरं पाट्यते तद् बाहुकण्टकं नाम युद्धम् Nī. on 12. 5. 4 (Bom. Ed.)].
बिभीषिका: Bibhīṣikā f.: A kind of माया used by the Gandharvas to frighten men. Arjuna told the Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa that the Bibhīṣikā employed by him had no effect on those who knew the use of the अस्त्रस्; if employed, it vanished like foam (अस्त्रज्ञेषु प्रयुक्तैषा फेनवत् प्रविली-यते) 1. 158. 24.
ब्रह्मदण्ड: Brahmadaṇḍa m.: A weapon of Brah-man (Nī., however, ब्रह्मदण्ड आभिचारि-कविद्या on 2. 5. 122, Bom. Ed.). Described as ‘very fierce’ (महाघोर), ‘having lustre like the fire on the Doom's Day’ (कालाग्निसमतेजस्) 1. 49. 24; Nārada asked Yudhiṣṭhira whether he knew the use of the Brahmadaṇḍa 2. 5. 111; one of the weapons placed by Śiva on his chariot when it was made ready for the fight with the Tripuras (other weapons placed on the chariot being Kāladaṇḍa, Rudradaṇḍa) 8. 24. 79; Brahma-daṇḍa used for various comparisons: (1) the शक्ति hurled by Yudhiṣṭhira at Śalya and which killed him was said to be ‘unfailing’ (अमोघा) like the Brahmadaṇḍa 9. 16. 42; (2) the arrows of Arjuna which struck Bhīṣma (6. 114. 57) had the touch of Brahma-daṇḍa (ब्रह्मदण्डसमस्पर्शाः); and the arrows with which Droṇa fought with Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna had the lustre of Brahmadaṇḍa (शरांश् च ब्रह्मदण्डाभान्) 7. 164. 122; the arrows of Rāma that killed Rāvaṇa looked like a raised Brahmadaṇḍa 3. 274. 27; (3) the गदा of Bhīma compared with a raised Brahmadaṇḍa 5. 50. 8; (4) Rāvaṇa hurled a शूल at Rāma which looked like a raised Brahmadaṇḍa 3. 274. 19; (5) Garuḍa, flying in the sky, appeared to Kaśyapa, his father, like a raised Brahmadaṇḍa 1. 26. 7; (6) enraged Sudhanvan, the son of Aṅgiras, looked like the burning Brahmadaṇḍa 2. 61. 62; (7) the fear of the sacrificial fire which the snake Vāsuki entertained due to his mother's curse compared with Brahmadaṇḍa 1. 49. 22-24; (1. 52. 22 ?); [Brahmadaṇḍa also means ‘punishment inflicted by the curse of a Brāhmaṇa’ 1. 2. 220; 16. 4. 38].
ब्रह्मशिरस्: Brahmaśiras1 nt.: Name of a missile (once called ब्रह्मास्त्र 10. 15. 21). A. History: Supposed to have arisen from Brahman's lustre (ब्रह्मतेजोभव 10. 15. 7); Droṇa, after practising severe austerities, received the missile Brahmaśiras from Agastya 10. 12. 14; later it was taught by Droṇa to Arjuna when he was satisfied (प्रितिमान्, प्रीयमाणः) with him (Arjuna) 1. 123. 72; 10. 12. 5 and, not with great delight (नातिहृष्टमनाः), to Aśvatthāman whom he had apparently first refused to teach 10. 12. 6. B. Description: powerful missile (पर-मास्त्र) 1. 123. 78; 10. 15. 3, 6; famous as ‘uncomparable’ in the worlds (असामान्यम् इदं तात लोकेष्व् अस्त्रं निगद्यते) 1. 123. 76; divine (दिव्य) 10. 15. 16; outstanding (विशिष्ट) 1. 123. 74; highly irresistible (अति-दुर्धर) 1. 123. 74; fiery (महार्चिष्मत्) 10. 14. 7; difficult to obtain (दुरवाप) 10. 15. 9; worshipped by gods and Gandharvas (देवगन्धर्वपूजित) 10. 12. 14; capable of burning the whole earth (दहेद् यद् पृथिवीम् अपि) 10. 12. 4. C. Restrictions on its use: (1) while giving the अस्त्र to Arjuna, Droṇa told him not to use it against men, but to use it only if he was attacked in a battle by a superhuman enemy (अमानुषः शत्रुः); if released against an enemy of lesser mettle (अल्पतेजस्), the missile would burn the world 1. 123. 75, 77; (2) while teaching it to Aśvatthāman, who was known to be rash by nature, Droṇa warned him not to use it even under dire circumstances in battle, espe-cially not against men (परमापद्गतेनापि न स्म तात त्वया रणे । इदम् अस्त्रं प्रयोक्तव्यं मानुषेषु विशेषतः) 10. 12. 7-8. D. Taught by Droṇa only to Arjuna and Aśvatthāman: (1) It was given to Arjuna since Droṇa considered him to be dis-tinguished among his pupils (विशिष्टं सर्व-शिष्येभ्यः) 1. 123. 72; 10. 15. 21; when taught to Arjuna, he would be an unrivalled archer (भविता त्वत्समो नान्यः पुमाल्̃ लोके धनुर्धरः) 1. 123. 78; Droṇa taught to Arjuna, both its use and withdrawal (सप्रयोगनिवर्तनम्) 1. 123. 74; its with-drawal very difficult; once released, no one except Arjuna, not even Indra, was capable of withdrawing it 10. 15. 5, 6; it could not be with-drawn by one who had not observed celibacy; if a non-qualified person tried to withdraw it, it would cut his head and destroy his belongings 10. 15. 7-8; Arjuna could with-draw it as he was truthful, brave, had prac-tised celibacy, and was obedient to his teacher 10. 15. 10, 20, 24; although fully qualified to withdraw it, Arjuna never used it in the epic war nor outside it, even under stress (ब्रह्मचारी व्रती चापि दुरवापम् अवाप्य तत् । परमव्यसनार्तो ऽपि नार्जुनो ऽस्त्रं व्यमुञ्चत) 10. 15. 9, (ब्रह्मास्त्रम् अप्य् अवाप्यैतद् … क्षत्रधर्मान् महाबाहुर् नाकम्पत धनंजयः) 10. 15. 21; (2) Envious of Arjuna, Aśvatthāman asked his father to teach him Brahmaśiras; Droṇa gave it to him but not with a pleased mind (नाति-हृष्टमना इव) 10. 12. 6; (since Aśvatthā-man could not make use of it) he wanted to exchange it with Kṛṣṇa for his (Sudarśana) Cakra so that Aśvatthāman could be invin-cible 10. 12. 15, 36; Kṛṣṇa offered to give any one of his weapons to Aśvatthāman with-out receiving from him in return his Brahma-śiras 10. 12. 18-19; Aśvatthāman chose the Cakra but failed even so much as to move it from its place 10. 12. 20-23. E. Use: As Aśvatthāman was cruel and rash, there was every danger of his using Brahmaśiras against Bhīma, who was chasing him 10. 12. 40; when Aśvatthāman actually used it on an इषीका, Kṛṣṇa advised Arjuna to release his Brahmaśiras to counter it; Arjuna got down from the chariot with bow and arrow in hand, wished ‘well’ (स्वस्ति 10. 14. 5; 1. 1. 155) first to Aśvatthāman, then to himself and to his brothers (the Pāṇḍavas); then bowing down to deities and teachers, he released Brahmaśiras, wishing welfare, and saying ‘may the missile pacify (Aśvatthā-man's) missile’ (उत्ससर्ज शिवं ध्यायन्न् अस्त्रम् अस्त्रेण शाम्यताम्) 10. 14. 4-6; 10. 15. 2, 20; 1. 1. 155; at that time fire broke out like the fire at the end of the aeon; the fire of Arjuna's missile matched the fire of Aśvat-thāman's missile; as a result terror struck the creatures, skies were filled with great sound and were engulfed in fire, earth, with its mountains and trees, shook; the two missiles produced heat with their lustre 10. 14. 7-11; just then Nārada and Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, de-siring welfare for all the people, appeared and stood between the two missiles; they pointed out that Brahmaśiras was never used by any one before against men 10. 14. 16; in response to their appeal, Arjuna immediately with-drew his Brahmaśiras; but Aśvatthāman could not 10. 15. 1-15; moreover, if Brahmaśiras was pacified by the other powerful missile (परमास्त्र) there would be no rain in the land for twelve years 10. 15. 23; Aśvatthā-man then directed his missile towards the foetus of the Pāṇḍavas 10. 15. 31, 32; 10. 16. 9. [See Iṣīkā, Brahmaśiras2, Brahmā-stra]

Brahmaśiras2 nt.: Name of the missile of Śiva (Rudra) (identified with the fierce (घोर), divine (दिव्य) Pāśupatāstra 3. 41. 7). A. Origin: It arose from अमृत 3. 89. 11; Rudra acquired it with austerities 3. 89. 10. B. Description: great (महत्) and unrivalled (अप्रतिम) 3. 89. 10, fierce, of terrible power (रौद्रं भीमपराक्र-मम्) 3. 41. 8; 3. 89. 11; it destroys the whole world at the time of the युगान्त 3. 41. 8. C. Given to Arjuna: Arjuna requested Śiva to give his Brahmaśiras (Pāśupata); armed with it, Arjuna wanted to burn in battle the Dānavas, the Rākṣasas, the Bhūtas, the Piśācas, the Gandharvas, and the Pannagas; using it Arjuna wanted to fight with Bhīṣma, Droṇa. Kṛpa, and Karṇa 3. 41. 8-11; Arjuna received it from Rudra together with the मन्त्रस् to be recited at the time of its employment, the mode of withdrawing it, and the benediction meant for expiation (if wrongly used) सम-न्त्रं ससंहारं सप्रायश्चित्तमङ्गलम् 3. 89. 11 (however, Nī. प्रायश्चित्तम् अस्त्रा-ग्निना निरपराधानां दाहे यो दोषस् तस्य शोधनम् । मङ्गलं दग्धानाम् एवारा-मादीनां पुनर्विकसनम् । on Bom. Ed. 3. 91. 12). D. Effect: When employed, thousands of शूलस्, गदास्, and serpent-like ‘charmed’ arrows came out of it (शराश् चाशीविषाकाराः संभवन्त्य् अनुमन्त्रिताः) 3. 41. 10. [See Pāśupata, Brahmaśiras1]

Brahmaśiras nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। On the river Bhāgīrathī; listed by Aṅgi-ras in the Tīrthavaṃśa 13. 26. 3; one who visits it, bathes in the Bhāgīrathī and fasts for one month obtains the Somaloka 13. 26. 38.
ब्रह्मास्त्र: Brahmāstra, Brāhma astra, (Paitā- maha) nt. (rarely pl. 7. 165. 22; 8. 29. 26): Name of a missile. A. Relationship with god Brahman: Destined by god Brahman for repulsing all other missiles (सर्वास्त्रप्रतिघाताय विहितं पद्मयोनिना) 7. 172. 32; when withdrawn by Kṛṣṇa from the stillborn Parikṣit, the flaming missile returned to Pitāmaha (Brahman) 14. 69. 1, 3. B. Gods and heroes who knew its use: (1) Among the gods, Indra knew it 5. 47. 100; (2) Among men: (i) Droṇa: He received it from Rāma Jāmadagnya; when Droṇa received it, he became distinguished among men 1. 154. 13; Droṇa not equalled by any one in the use of Brahmāstra; Drupada attributed his defeat at the hands of Droṇa to Droṇa's know-ledge of Brahmāstra 1. 155. 22; Droṇa un-equalled in battle by any one because of his knowledge of Brahmāstra (and other missiles) ( … ब्रह्मास्त्रादीनि यान्य् अपि । तानि सर्वाणि तिष्ठन्ति भवत्य् एव विशेषतः) 7. 160. 5; known for his knowledge of Brahmāstra, Droṇa knew its use and remedy (सप्रयोग-चिकित्सितम्) 3. 38. 5; 4. 46. 7, 9; 7. 166. 2; (ii) Arjuna: He was taught (निष्ठित) Brāhma astra by his teacher (Droṇa) 1. 181. 20; 6. 116. 38; in its use, he never violated the rules of the Kṣatriyas (क्षत्र-धर्मान् महाबाहुर् नाकम्पत धनं-जयः) 10. 15. 21; Arjuna was asked by Indra to learn the Paitāmaha astra (identical, or different from Brahmāstra ?) 3. 164. 29; (iii-v) Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, and Aśvatthāman: According to Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma, Kṛpa and Aśvatthāman knew its use and remedy (स-प्रयोगचिकित्सितम्) 3. 38. 5; 4. 46. 7 (Kṛpa and Aśvatthāman); 4. 46. 9 (Aśvatthāmān); (vi) Karṇa: Karṇa requested Droṇa to teach him Brahmāstra together with its secret and withdrawal, but Droṇa refused to oblige 12. 2. 10, 13; Karṇa, who coveted the Astra (12. 3. 27, 30), then learnt it in its entirety (कृत्स्नम्) from Rāma Jāmadagnya 12. 3. 2; 8. 5. 67; but since Karṇa had told a lie to obtain its knowledge (12. 3. 30), Rāma cursed him saying that the missile would flash to him on all occasions except when he met his equal and the time of his death had arrived (ते … ब्रह्मास्त्रं प्रतिभास्यति । अन्यत्र वधकातात् ते सदृशेन समेयुषः) 12. 3. 30-31; 5. 61. 2; returning, Karṇa reported to Duryodhana that he had acquired the missiles (from Rāma) (कृतास्त्रो ऽस्मि) 12. 3. 33; since Karṇa had pacified Rāma, knowledge of Brahmāstra remained with him; hence Karṇa assured Duryodhana that he was quite capable of bearing the burden of the war (ततस् तद् अस्त्रं मम सावशेषं तस्मात् समर्थो ऽस्मि ममैष भारः) 5. 61. 2-4; according to Yudhiṣṭhira, Karṇa knew the use and remedy of Brahmāstra 3. 38. 5; Karṇa boasted to Śalya that he knew the Brāhma astras (pl. अस्त्राणि … ब्राह्माणी) 8. 29. 26; (vii) Kṛṣṇa: According to Bhīṣma, perhaps Kṛṣṇa knew Brāhma and many other heavenly weapons (कृष्णो वा देवकी-पुत्रः) 6. 116. 39; (viii) Vibhīṣaṇa: He prayed Brahman that the Brahmāstra might flash to him although it was not duly taught to him (अशिक्षितं च भगवन् ब्रह्मास्त्रं प्रतिभातु मे) 3. 259. 30; [For its use also by Yudhiṣṭhira, Kuvalāśva, Bṛhatkṣatra, Pradyumna, Rāma (Dāśarathi), and Lakṣ-maṇa see below section F]. C. Des-cription: heavenly (दिव्य) 3. 271. 16; 7. 101. 12; 7. 160. 5; 7. 165. 22, 105; 8. 29. 27; 9. 61. 13, (19); great missile (महास्त्र) 3. 163. 33; 7. 165. 23; 8. 65. 23; (परम् अस्त्रम्) 8. 66. 52; (परमास्त्र) 5. 185. 15; best (उत्तम) 5. 185. 16; unrivalled (अप्र-तिम) 8. 29. 27; dreadful (घोर) 3. 274. 27, (माहाघोर) 8. 5. 67; fierce (उग्र) 8. 65. 23; unbearable (असह्य) 8. 65. 24; of un-matched strength (अप्रतिमौजस्) 3. 274. 27; invincible even in thought (मनसा तद् ध्य् अजय्यम्) 8. 29. 27; highly respected (परमसंमत) 1. 154. 13; to be employ-ed mentally (मनसा संविधेयम्) 8. 65. 24; cannot be withstood even by Indra 9. 61. 27. D. Teaching of the अस्त्र: The use of the missile was to be taught in full (कृत्स्नम्), i. e. together with the mode of its withdrawal; this is how Rāma Jāmadagnya taught it to Karṇa after performing due rites (तस्मै स विधिवत् कृत्स्नम् ब्रह्मास्त्रं सनिवर्तनम् । प्रोवाच) 12. 3. 2; Droṇa learnt from Rāma Jāmadagnya both—the mode of its employment (प्रयोग) and with-drawal (संहार) 1. 154. 11; when Karṇa expressed his desire to learn it from Droṇa he wanted to know it with its secrets and the mode of its withdrawal (सरहस्यनिवर्तनम्) 12. 2. 10; Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa and Aśvatthāman reputed for their knowledge of the employment of the अस्त्र and its remedy (i. e. withdrawal) (सप्रयोगचिकित्सितम्) 3. 38. 5; it could be taught only to a Brāh-maṇa who had duly observed the prescribed vow (यथावत् चरितव्रतः), or a Kṣatriya who had practised austerities (तपस्वी), but to none else 12. 2. 13; hence Karṇa told a lie to Rāma Jāmadagnya about his lineage while declaring that he was a Bhārgava Brāh-maṇa 12. 2. 15; 12. 3. 26-30. E. Use and withdrawal: At the time of its employ-ment, मन्त्रस् related to Brahmāstra were recited on an arrow to use it as a charged missile (बाणवर्यं … ब्रह्मास्त्रेणाभि-मन्त्रितम्) 3. 274. 24-25; (ब्रह्मास्त्र-परिमन्त्रितैः सायकैः) 3. 167. 17; (सं-मन्त्र्य) 8. 66. 52; these मन्त्रस् used to charge the arrow with the Brāhma (and the other अस्त्रस्) were supposed to serve as the ritual मन्त्रस् for the ‘sacrifice to be performed with weapons’ (शस्त्रयज्ञ, i. e. in the war) 5. 139. 31; it was necessary to support the bow and the arrow with great might (बलेनाथ स संस्तभ्य ब्रह्मा-स्त्रं समुदैरयत्) 8. 66. 48; at the time of withdrawing the Brahmāstra (Iṣīkā) employ-ed by Aśvatthāman, Kṛṣṇa touched water (उपस्पृश्य) 14. 68. 16, 14. 69. 1, and also made a सत्यक्रिया 14. 68. 19-23. F. Uses: (1) In the epic war: (i) by Droṇa—(a) against Arjuna in order to cut down the भल्ल arrows 7. 67. 9 (समु-दीरय-); 7. 163. 43 (प्रादुष्कृ-); 9. 61. 27; (b) against Yudhiṣṭhira to burn his शक्ति to ashes 7. 81. 32-33 (प्रादुष्कृ-); 7. 132. 33 (उदीरय-); (c) against Bṛhat-kṣatra of the Kekayas 7. 101. 12 (प्रा-दुष्कृ-); (d) against the Pāñcālas, killing twenty thousand chariot-fighters, besides many elephants and horses 7. 164. 79-83 (प्रादुष्कृ-); in addition, Droṇa killed ten अयुतस् of the Pāñcāla soldiers with Brāhma astra as if to destroy all the Kṣatriyas (क्षत्रियाणाम् अभावाय ब्राह्मम् आत्मानम् आस्थितः) 7. 165. 14-15; (e) against the armies of the Pāṇḍavas, the Kekayas, the Matsyas, specially of the Pāñcālas killing by hundreds and thousands; Droṇa also burnt one thousand chariot-fighters and two thousand elephant-riders 7. 165. 100-102; (f) against Dhṛṣṭadyumna while dashing the horses of his chariot against those of Dhṛṣṭadyumna (ब्राह्मम् अस्त्रम् उदीरयन्) 7. 164. 129; (उदीरयेतां ब्राह्माणि दिव्यान्य् अस्त्राण्य् अनेकशः) 7. 165. 22; (ब्राह्मम् अस्त्रं विकुर्वाणः) 7. 165. 100; (दिव्यम् अस्त्रं विकुर्वाणः) 7. 165. 105; (ii) by Arjuna: (a) He assured Kṛṣṇa that by employing his Brāhma astra he would repulse all the missiles used against him by the protectors of Jaya-dratha 7. 53. 44; (b) Arjuna cut down with the rain of arrows released by the use of the Brahmāstra the shower of arrows released against him by Droṇa by using the same mis-sile 7. 67. 12; 7. 163. 46; (c) Arjuna released (उदीरय-) his Brāhma astra to nullify the effect of the Āgneya astra (7. 172. 14) of Aśvatthāman 7. 172. 14; (d) against Karṇa: Arjuna thought of using it for the welfare of the people (शिवाय लोकस्य) and the death of Karṇa (वधाय सौतेः); to do this he sought the permission of Kṛṣṇa, the gods, Brahman, Śiva, and of all the knowers of ब्रह्मन् (ब्र-ह्मविद्) 8. 65. 23-24; Arjuna advised to use Brahmāstra by Kṛṣṇa 8. 66. 52 (विसृज्-, प्रयो-जय।); he countered Karṇa's Brahmāstra by using apparently the same missile (तद् अस्त्रम् अस्त्रेणावार्य) 8. 67. 8; (iii) by Karṇa: (a) when he was surrounded at once by many Pāṇḍava warriors 8. 33. 25 (उदीरय-); (b) against Arjuna 8. 66. 48 (समुदीरय-); 8. 67. 8; (9. 61. 27); (iv) by Yudhiṣṭhira: to pacify the Brahmāstra of Droṇa used against him 7. 81. 34; 7. 132. 35; (v) by Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna: He and Droṇa used (उदीरय-) heavenly Brāhma missiles (pl.) against each other in many ways (ब्राह्माणि दिव्यान्य् अस्त्राण्य् अनेकशः) 7. 165. 22; Dhṛṣṭdyumna repelled successfully all missiles used by Droṇa 7. 165. 23; (vi) by Bṛhatkṣatra (a Kaikeya): he repulsed Droṇa's Brāhma astra by the use of the same weapon 7. 101. 13, (14); (2) Outside the epic war: (i) by Arjuna: (a) against Kirāta (Śiva); but it was destroyed by Kirāta 3. 163. 33, 35; (b) against the Nivātakavacas to blow them away by hundreds and thousands with the arrows released from the missile 3. 167. 17; (ii) by Aśvatthāman: the इषीका directed by Aśvatthāman towards the foetus of Uttarā (10. 15. 31, 33) identified with Brahmāstra 14. 65. 9; 14. 67. 21; 14. 68. 16; 14. 69. 1; (14. 67. 13, 16); (iii) by Rāma Jāmadagnya: he used it against Bhīṣma 5. 185. 15 (प्रादुष्कृ-); (iv) by Bhīṣma: to counter with the same missile the use of the Brahmāstra by Rāma Jāmadagnya 5. 185. 16 (प्रयुज्-); (v) by Pradyumna: against Śālva to cut off half way his Daiteyāstra (माया) 3. 20. 17; (vi) by Kuvalāśva: against the Daitya Dhundhu who was burnt with it 3. 195. 28; (vii) by Rāma (Dāśa-rathi): against Rāvaṇa; Rāma, while using it, recited मन्त्रस् on his arrow; with it, Rāvaṇa, together with his chariot and the charioteer, were burnt down 3. 274. 24-25, 28; (viii) by Lakṣmaṇa: against the demon Kumbhakarṇa who was burnt with it 3. 271. 16. G. Effects of Brahmāstra: When the Brahmāstra was released: (i) it produced a very large number of (flaming) arrows 3. 163. 33; 3. 167. 17; 7. 67. 9 (भल्ल), 12; 7. 165. 100 (भल्ल); 8. 33. 25; 8. 65. 24; 8. 66. 53; 8. 67. 8; (ii) it produced fire enough to heat the worlds and fill the directions and space with lustre (ततः संतापितो लोको मत्प्रसूतेन तेजसा । क्षणेन हि दिशः खं च सर्वतो ऽभिविदीपितम्) 3. 163. 34; (जज्वाल) 5. 185. 16; (व्योम्नि पादुर्-अभूत् तेजः) 5. 185. 18; (दीपयां चक्रे) 5. 186. 7; (तद् अस्त्रं ज्वलितम्) 14. 69. 3; or to burn the enemy with it 3. 195. 28; 3. 271. 16; 3. 274. 28; 7. 165. 102; or to burn the enemy's weapon 7. 81. 33; or to burn the enemy's chariot 9. 61. 18-19; or to burn the chariot together with horses and charioteer 3. 274. 28; (iii) it produced smoke to fill the directions 5. 185. 21; (iv) it produced darkness all over which terrified creatures 7. 132. 33-34; (v) it removed the darkness produced by the enemy's missile with the result that cold winds blew and the directions became clear 7. 172. 32; (vi) all life could be threatened by it 5. 47. 101; 5. 185. 18, 20-21; 7. 163. 45; (vii) earth, with its mountains, forests, and trees shook, winds blew in the opposite direction, and the oceans were agitated 7. 163. 44; 5. 185. 22; (viii) gods and other divine and demoniac beings were heated with its blaze 5. 185. 19; or they could not remain in the mid-region and they bewailed 5. 185. 21-22; (ix) under its influence the Rakṣases infested the residence; they disappeared when the missile was with-drawn 14. 69. 2. H. Withdrawal: Bra-hmāstra, when employed, either served the purpose for which it was used, or was repulsed, or pacified by the counter-use of the same missile (cf. above sections F and G); it was only once destroyed by Kirāta (Śiva) 3. 163. 35; only once when the same missile was employed by the opponents they clashed in-between without reaching the respective targets 5. 185. 17; Arjuna withdrew it (= Brahma-śiras) 10. 15. 1, 5, but it (Iṣīkā identified with Brahmāstra) could not be withdrawn by Aśvatthāman as he had not observed the ब्रह्मचारिव्रत 10. 15. 7-8; later Kṛṣṇa withdrew it after sipping water (and making a सत्यक्रिया) to revive the still-born child 14. 68. 16, (19-23); 14. 69. 1; when Kṛṣṇa withdrew the Brahmāstra, brilliant light emanated from the body of Parikṣit to fill the room; the evil spirits (रक्षांसि) then left the house and disappeared, and the mid-region was filled with the words ‘well-done’ (साधु केशव साध्व् इति) 14. 69. 1-2. I. Com-parison: the missile compared with the raised Brahmadaṇḍa 3. 274. 27; J. Status: Inferior to Pāśupatāstra of Śiva 13. 14. 127, (124). [See Iṣīkā, Brahmaśiras1]
बकवध: Bakavadha m.: Name of the 10th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 36, 33, 70. Mentioned in the narration of the con-tents of the Ādiparvan (बकस्य निधनं चैव) and referred to in the summary of the events made by Vaiśaṃpāyana for Jana-mejaya 1. 55. 21; related to the अध्यायस् 1. 143-152.
बाहुदन्तक: Bāhudantaka nt.: Name of a शास्त्र in the form of an abridgement made by Indra 12. 59. 89. The Nītiśāstra originally composed by Lokapitāmaha (Brahmadeva) was first abridged by Śiva and was then called Vaiśālākṣa; Indra received it in this form and abridged it further to five thousand अध्यायस्; it was called Bāhudantaka 12. 59. 88-89. [See Paitāmahaśāstra, Bārhas-patya, Vaiśālākṣa]
बृहस्पतिमत: Bṛhaspatimata nt.: Name of a Śāstra 12. 322. 43; referred to as बृहस्पतेर् मतम् in 12. 122. 11. The Śāstra was originally composed by the seven sages (Marīci, Atri and others 12. 322. 27) dealing with धर्म, अर्थ, काम, and subsequently with मोक्ष and other regulations (तत्र धर्मार्थकामा हि मोक्षः पश्चाच् च कीर्तितः । मर्यादा विवि-धाश् चैव 12. 322. 30); Manu Svāyaṃbhuva, and Uśanas and Bṛhaspati when the two would be born, were to propound the शास्त्र of the seven sages; the शास्त्र will be received by king Vasu 12. 322. 26-30; 35-37; 41-44; it was studied, along with the Auśanasa śāstra, also by king Vasuhoma of the Aṅgas; hence king Māndhātṛ asked Vasuhoma to tell him how दण्ड came into existence and how afterwards it came to be established among the Kṣatriyas (तद् अहं श्रोतुम् इच्छामि दण्ड उत्पद्यते कथम् ।  … कथं क्षत्रियसंस्थश् च दण्डः संप्रत्य् अवस्थितः) 12. 122. 11-13. [See Auśanasa]
ब्रह्मसूत्र: Brahmasūtra nt.: Name of a सूत्र-text ? The sages in ancient times are said to have sung individually in the Brahma-sūtra in different metres and with words which provide well-determined grounds their observations (viz. that this body is known as क्षेत्र and one who knows it is known as क्षेत्रज्ञ; and the Bhagavān is the क्षेत्रज्ञ residing in all क्षेत्रस् 6. 35. 1-2) 6. 35. 4 (ऋषिभिर् बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर् विविधैः पृथक् । ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश् चैव हेतुमद्भिर् विनिश्चितैः).
ब्रह्मोपनिसद्: Brahmopanisad f.: Name of a text (?) (or ‘a secret doctrine related to ब्रह्मन्’ ?) At the end of the war, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, when he met the sage Vyāsa, learnt it, along with the duties of a king 15. 43. 2-3 (स राजा राजधर्मांश् च ब्रह्मोपनिषदं तथा । अवाप्तवान् नरश्रेष्ठः … धृतराष्ट्रः समासाद्य व्यासं चापि तपस्विनम् ॥ ).
बुध: Budha m.: Name of a planet (Mer-cury). A. Importance: Budha, along with other planets, visits the सभा of Brahmadeva 2. 11. 20; mentioned, along with other planets, in the Daivatavaṃśa 13. 151. 12. B. Name of Sūrya: Budha appears as the 24th name among the 108 names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 19. C. Smile: (1) Droṇa and and Arjuna confronted each other in battle like Budha and Śukra in the sky 6. 97. 57; (2) The confronting of Duḥśāsana and Prativindhya appeared like that of Budha and Bhārgava (i. e. Śukra) in a cloudless sky 7. 143. 30; (3) Dhṛṣṭaketu and Bāhlīka fought each other like angry Aṅgāraka (Mars) and Budha 6. 43. 38; (4) Abhimanyu and Citrasena, when they met each other on the battlefield, shone like Budha and Śanaiścara in the sky 6. 100. 20; (5) Arjuna, marching out on his excellent chariot in the company of Kṛṣṇa and Sātyaki looked like moon, accompanied by Budha and Śukra, destroying the darkness 7. 60. 20. [For Budha also see Section 1. 7]
बृहस्पति: Bṛhaspati m.: Name of a planet (Jupiter), also called Guru (12. 139. 15). A. Description: Very bright (प्रज्व-लित) 6. 3. 25. B. Importance: Bṛhas-pati, along with other planets, visits the सभा of Brahmadeva 2. 11. 20; Bṛhaspati, with other planets, finds place in the Daivata-vaṃśa 13. 151. 12. C. Name of Sūrya: Bṛhaspati appears as the 22nd name among the 108 names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 19. D. Bad omen: (1) Among the bad omens pointed out by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra one was related to Bṛhaspati making retrograde movement in the constella-tion Śravaṇa (मघास्व् अङ्गारको वक्रः श्रवणे च बृहस्पतिः) 6. 3. 13; (2) The other omen observed by Vyāsa was that the planets Bṛhaspati and Śanaiścara were stationed near the two stars Viśākhā and were in that position for a year (संवत्स-रस्थायिनौ च ग्रहौ प्रज्वलिताव् उभौ । विशाखयोः समीपस्थौ बृहस्पतिशनैश्च-रौ) 6. 3. 25 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 27: पूर्वं श्रवणस्थो बृहस्पतिर् (reference to 6. 3. 13) भगनक्षत्रस्थः सूर्यपुत्र (reference to 6. 3. 14) इत्य् उक्तम् । ताव् उभौ विशाखासमीपे तिर्यग्वेधेन शत-पदे चक्रे विशाखानक्षत्रं विध्यत इत्य् अर्थः); (3) At the time of the death of Karṇa, Bṛhaspati afflicted Rohiṇī constellation and looked like moon and sun (बृहस्पती रोहिणीं संप्रपीड्य बभूव चन्द्रार्क-समानवर्णः) 8. 68. 49. E. Events connected with Bṛhaspati: (1) Formerly, when the Tretā was about to end and the Dvāpara was about to commence, as the Guru (Bṛhaspati) was not favourable it did not rain for twelve years (न ववर्ष सह-स्राक्षः प्रतिलोमो ऽभवद् गुरुः) 12. 139. 15, 13-14; (2) Mārkaṇḍeya told the Pāṇḍa-vas that when the moon, the sun, the Tiṣya (Puṣya) and Bṛhaspati will come together in the same sign of the zodiac (राशि), the Kṛtayuga will commence (यदा चन्द्रश् च सूर्यश् च तथा तिष्यबृहस्पती । एकराशौ समेष्यन्ति प्रपत्स्यति तदा कृतम्) 3. 188. 87 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 190. 90: गुरुसूर्यचन्द्राः यदा युगपत् पुष्य-नक्षत्रम् एष्यन्ति तदा कृतयुगप्रवृत्तिर् इत्य् अर्थः). [For Bṛhaspati see Section 1. 7]
ब्रह्मकल्प: Brahmakalpa m.: A cosmic period of Brahman. In a former Brahmakalpa, when the ब्रह्मर्षिस् met, they entertained doubt about the creation of the world (ब्रह्मकल्पे पुरा ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मर्षीणां समागमे । लोकसंभवसन्देहः समुत्पन्नो महात्-मनाम्) 12. 176. 6.
ब्रह्मराशि: Brahmarāśi m.: Name of a constellation (identical with Śravaṇa ?). One of the bad omens pointed out by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra was related to the planet Mars who made repeated retrograde movements and then returned to Brahmarāśī to remain steady in the constellation Śra-vaṇa (वक्रानुवक्रं कृत्वा च श्रवणे पावकप्रभः । ब्रह्मराशिं समावृत्य लोहिताङ्गो व्यवस्थितः ॥ 6. 3. 17) (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 18: तत्रैव सर्वतोभद्र-चक्रे मघास्थो लोहिताङ्गो ऽङ्गारको वक्रा-नुवक्रं कृत्वा पुनःपुनर् वक्रीभूय ब्रह्मणा बृहस्पतिनाक्रान्तं राशिं नक्षत्रम् श्रवणं समावृत्य सम्यक् पूऋनदृष्ट्या विद्ध्वा तिष्ठति).
ब्राह्म: Brāhma1, (Brāhmī f.) adj.: of the day and night of Brahman. A day and night each of Brahman is equal to one thousand Yugas (a Yuga or a Kalpa being equal to twelve thousand years which is the total duration of the Kṛta, the Tretā, the Dvāpara and the Kali taken together) (एषा द्वादशसाहस्री युगाख्या परिकीर्तिता ॥ एतत् सहस्रपर्यन्तम् अहो ब्राह्मम् उदाहृतम्) 3. 186. 22-23; 12. 224. 28; 12. 224. 17; सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तम् अहर् यद् ब्रह्मणो विदुः । रात्रिं युगस-हस्रान्तां ते ऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥ ) 6. 30. 17 = 12. 224. 30; at the beginning of his night, i. e. during the Pralaya, Brahman enters into himself and sleeps; at the end of the night he is awakened from his sleep and creates the great भूत (i. e. Hiraṇya-garbha) (रात्रिस् तावत्तिथी ब्राह्मी तदादौ विश्वम् ईश्वरः । प्रलये ऽध्यात्मम् आविश्य सुप्त्वा सो ऽन्ते विबुध्यते ॥ प्रतिबुद्धो विकुरुते ब्रह्माक्षय्यं क्षपाक्षये । सृजते च महद् भूतम्) 12. 224. 29, 31; (सृजत्य् अनन्तकर्माणं महान्तं भू-तम् अग्रजम्) 12. 291. 15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 302. 15: अग्रजं हिरण्यगर्भम्); युगं द्वादशसाहस्रं कल्पं विद्धि चतुर्गुणम् । दशकल्पशतावृत्तं तद् अहर् ब्राह्मम् उच्यते । रात्रिश् चैतावती राजन् यस्यान्ते प्रतिबुध्यते 12. 291. 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 302. 14: तद् एव चतुर्युगं दशशतावृत्तं कल्पं तद् एव च ब्राह्मम् अहर् उच्यते); at the end of Brahman's night there arises due to the kindness of the god of boundless lustre (i. e. of god Nārāyaṇa 12. 328. 12) a lotus, where again by the god's kindness Brahman is born; at the end of Brahman's day, from the forehead of the god, who is angry, arises his son, Rudra, the destroyer (ब्राह्मे रात्रिक्षये प्राप्ते तस्य ह्य् अमिततेजसः । प्रसादात् प्रादुरभवत् पद्मं पद्म-निभेक्षण । तत्र ब्रह्मा समभवत् स तस्यैव प्रसादतः ॥ अह्नः क्षये ललाटाच् च सुतो देवस्य वै तथा । क्रोधाविष्टस्य संजज्ञे रुद्रः संहारकारकः) 12. 328. 15-16; at the beginning of the Brahman's day all manifestations arise from the non-manifest; at the beginning of his night the manifestations are dissolved into the same non-manifest (अव्यक्ताद् व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्य् अहरागमे । रात्र्यागमे प्र-लीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके) 6. 30. 18.

Brāhma2 adj.: of a मुहूर्त (time before sunrise, early morning). A. Epic event: when Arjuna sat on the ground and mentally thought of Bhava, he, at the auspicious ब्राह्म मुहूर्त, with his (mind) concentrated, saw himself in the sky in the company of Keśava (भूमाव् आसीन एकाग्रो जगाम मनसा भवम् ॥ ततः प्रणिहिते ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते शुभलक्-षणे । आत्मानम् अर्जुनो ऽपश्यद् गगने सहकेश्वम् ॥ ) 7. 57. 19-20 (Nī. who reads प्रणिहितो (Bom. Ed. 7. 80. 23) explains समाहितमनाः). B. Time for perfor-ming the संध्या ceremony: Bhīṣma advised Yudhiṣṭhira that one who wanted long life should wake up at the ब्राह्म मुहूर्त, think of धर्म and काम (the two पुरुषार्थस्), and after sipping water for purification, should, with folded hands, perform the first संध्या (ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते बुध्येत धर्मार्थौ चानुचिन्तयेत् । उत्था-याचम्य तिष्ठेत पूर्वां संध्यां कृताञ्-जलिः ॥ ) 13. 107. 16.
Brāhma nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। It is supposed to exist in the middle space of the thumb (अङ्गुष्ठस्यान्तराले च ब्राह्-मं तीर्थम् उदाहृतम्) 13. 107. 96.
बदरपाचन: Badarapācana, Badarīpācana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Explanation of the name: The तीर्थ so called because Indra asked Srucāvatī to cook jujube berries there (पचस्वैतानि सुभगे बदराणि) 9. 47. 16; Arundhatī in the bygone days tasted and cooked jujube fruits there for twelve years as told by Mahādeva (ततो ऽब्रवीन् महादेवः पच-स्वैतानि (i. e. बदराणि) सुव्रते) 9. 47. 34-37. 42; Arundhatī expressed there her wish that the तीर्थ be known as Badarapācana (तीर्थं स्याद् इदं … नाम्ना बदरपाच-नम्) 9. 47. 44. B. Description: Auspicious (शुभ) 9. 46. 29; 9. 47. 28; best (उत्तम) 9. 47. 44; excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थवर) 9. 47. 1, 27, 28; removing all sins (सर्वपापा-पह) 9. 47. 27; famous in the three worlds (विख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु) 9. 47. 27; perma-nent in the world (स्थिरं लोके) 9. 47. 27; inhabited by all kinds of beings (निषेवितं सर्वसत्त्वैः) 9. 46. 29; dear to the Siddhas, gods and sages (सिद्धदेवर्षिदयित) 9. 47. 44; frequented by ascetics and the Siddhas (तपस्विसिद्धचरित) 9. 47. 1; thronged by Brahmanical seers (ब्रह्मर्षिभिर् अभिप्लु-तम्) 9. 47. 27; (having trees that are) always flowering and bearing fruits (सदा-पुष्पफल) 9. 46. 29; having forests bloom-ing in different seasons (नानर्तुकवनोपेत) 9. 46. 29. C. Holiness: (i) One who is well composed (सुसमाहितः) if he lives there for a night and bathes in the तीर्थ he gets after death worlds that are difficult to obtain (लोकान् … दुर्लभान्) 9. 47. 51; (2) One who is pure (शुचिः) if he lives there for three nights observing fast he obtains fruit of fasting for twelve years 9. 47. 45; (3) One should fast there for three nights and then eat Badara berries; if one eats only Badara berries for twelve years that is equal to fasting for three nights 3. 81. 157. D. Events: (1) Epic: Balarāma visited the तीर्थ 9. 46. 28-29; 9. 47. 1; he bathed (उपस्पृश्य) there and gave riches to great Brāhmaṇas 9. 47. 61; (2) Past: (i) Srucāvatī, the beautiful daughter of Bharadvāja, practised severe austerities to obtain the king of gods (Indra) for her husband 9. 47. 2-3; (also see section A above); (ii) The seven sages left Arundhatī at this तीर्थ and went to the Himavant 9. 47. 28. [See Badarikātīrtha]
बदरिकातीर्थ: Badarikātīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who has subdued his mind (प्रयत-मानसः), if he bathes there he gets long life and goes to heaven 3. 83. 13. [See Badara-pācana]
बलाका: Balākā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Mentioned in the Tīrthavaṃśa proclaim-ed by Aṅgiras; one who bathes there (कृतोद-कः) becomes famous among gods and shines with his fame (देवेषु कीर्तिं लभते यशसा च विराजते) 13. 26. 18.
बहिर्गिरि: Bahirgiri m.: Name of a mountain (?) Situated in the north; it was conquered by Arjuna in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya 2. 24. 2, 1.
बहुला: Bahulā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 26, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
बाहुदा: Bāhudā1 f.: Name of a river. In the east 3. 85. 3, 22; flowing, along with the river Nandā, from the mountain Kuṇḍoda (बाहुदा च नदी यत्र नन्दा च गिरिमूर्धनि) 3. 85. 20-21; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhārata-varṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 28, 13 (for other details see Bahulā); the Pāṇḍavas in their तीर्थयात्रा bathed in this river (चक्रुः सर्वे ऽभिषेचनम्) 3. 93. 4. [See Bāhudā2]

Bāhudā2 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: In the north, on the moun-tain Himavant 13. 20. 3; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 13. B. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 12. 24. 23; 13. 20. 3; great river (महानदी) 13. 151. 22; conferring the reward of performing one's religious duties (धर्मदायिनी) 13. 20. 3; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Name justified: Likhita, whose hands were cut off as punishment for the sin of eating without permission fruits in the आश्रम of his brother Śaṅkha, received his hands back when he bathed in the river Bāhudā (अव-गाह्यापगां पुण्याम् … प्रादुरास्तां ततस् तस्य करौ) 12. 24. 23-24. D. Holi-ness: (1) If one who observes chastity and is composed (ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः) visits the river he gets the fruit of performing a Devasatra sacrifice (देवसत्रस्य यज्ञस्य फलम् आप्नोति मानवः) 3. 82. 60; (2) Those who visit the river Bāhudā become holy and obtaining divine form and wearing heave-nly garlands and rich in holy fragrance they delight in the Goloka (? गवां विमाने) 13. 105. 45, 48, 44 (for citation see Karatoyinī). E. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2. F. Limitation: Giving cows in very large num-bers on the river Bāhudā (गवां शतानाम् अयुतम्) is highly meritorious no doubt; but it is not enough to take one to Brahmaloka 13. 106. 37, 7. G. Past events: (1) The two brothers Śaṅkha and Likhita had esta-blished their attractive आश्रमस् along the river Bāhudā 12. 24. 3; Śaṅkha advised Likhita, when the latter's hands were cut off as punishment, to go to the river Bāhudā and gratify according to the rites (यथा-विधि) gods, manes and sages and never again think of committing an अधर्म 12. 24. 22; (2) Aṣṭāvakra reached this river when he, as advised by the sage Vadānya, went to the north to see an old ascetic lady; he bathed in the तीर्थ on this river and gratified the deities and spent a night there 13. 20. 3-5; 13. 19. 24. [See Bāhudā1]
बिन्दुसरस्: Bindusaras nt.: Name of a lake. A. Location: In the north-east (प्राग्-उदीचीम् अगाद् दिशम्) 2. 3. 7; on the moun-tain Hiraṇyaśṛṅga (or Hiraṇyaśikhara), near the mountain Maināka, to the north of the Kailāsa (उत्तरेण तु कैलासं मैनाकं पर्वतं प्रति । हिरण्यशृङ्गः … गिरिः॑ रम्यं बिन्दुसरो नाम) 2. 3. 8-9, 2; (हिरण्यशिखरं चैव तच् च बिन्दुसरः) 3. 145. 39-41; near this lake the river Tri-pathagā (Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā), issuing from Brahmaloka, got divided into seven streams 6. 7. 44. B. Description: Pleasing (रम्य) 2. 3. 2, 9; 6. 7. 41; auspicious (शिव) 3. 145. 39; (शुभ) 6. 7. 41; hea-venly (दिव्य) 6. 7. 41; large (महत्) 6. 7. 41; having golden sand (काञ्चनवालुक) 6. 7. 41. C. Epic events: (1) Asura Maya wanted to go to Bindusaras to bring the pot of jewels to construct the Sabhā for the Pāṇḍavas 2. 3. 2-4; he went there and collected the गदा of Yauvanāśva which he thought was suitable for Bhīma, the big conch of Varuṇa, called Devadatta, for Arjuna, and the crystals used for Vṛṣa-parvan's Sabhā; he brought these to Indra-prastha with the help of his Rakṣas servants 2. 3. 5-7, 16 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 2. 3. 19: किंकरैः रक्षसां जातिविशेषैः); (2) Maya built a lotus pond with jewels brought from Bindusaras and covered it with crystals (कृतां बिन्दुसरोरत्नैर् मयेन स्फाटिकच्छदाम् । … नलिनीम्) 2. 46. 26. D. Past and mythological events: (1) Vṛṣa-parvan had a Sabhā made of crystals built for him there 2. 3. 16; Asura Maya had collected jewels in a pot in the Sabhā of Vṛṣaparvan when all the Dānavas offered a sacrifice near Bindusaras (यक्ष्यमानेषु सर्वेषु दानवेषु तदा मया । कृतं मणि-मयं भाण्डं रम्यं बिन्दुसरः प्रति ॥ ) 2. 3. 2-3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 3. 3: भाण्डम् इव भाण्डं मूलधनं विचित्ररङ्गोपादानद्रव्यं कृतं हिङ्गुला-दिवन् निर्मितम् मणिमयं मणिप्रचु-रम्); (2) Yauvanāśva, after killing his enemies, left his गदा near Bindusaras 2. 3. 5; (3) Varuṇa's big conch Devadatta was also left there 2. 3. 7; (4) Bhagīratha lived there for many years watching the river Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā 2. 3. 9; 6. 7. 41; (5) The god of all beings (i. e. Prajāpati) performed a hundred principal sacrifices there (यत्रेष्ट्वा सर्वभूतानाम् ईश्वरेण महात्मना । आहृताः क्रतवो मुख्याः शतं भरत-सत्तम ॥ ) 2. 3. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 3. 11: ईश्वरेण प्रजापतिना); (6) Indra obtained there perfection (सिद्धि) by per-forming a sacrifice 2. 3. 12; 6. 7. 42; (7) The eternal Bhūtapati (Mahādeva) created there all the worlds and is waited upon by thousands of Bhūtas 2. 3. 12; 6. 7. 43 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 3. 14: भूतपतिर् महादेवः); (8) There Vāsudeva constantly performed with faith सत्रस् lasting for a thousand years in order to convince the learn-ed (about the necessity of performing sacri-fices) (यत्रेष्टं वासुदेवेन सत्रैर् वर्ष-सहस्रकैः । श्रद्दधानेन सततम् शिष्ट-संप्रतिपत्तये ॥ ) 2. 3. 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 3. 16: शिष्टसंप्रतिपत्तये … शिष्टान् धर्मानुष्ठाने प्रवर्तयितुम्); at these सत्रस् the sacrificial poles were decorated with golden garlands and the altars were made of bright gold; Keśava gave (दक्षिणा) by thou-sands and millions (ददौ यत्र सहस्राणी प्रयुतानि च केशवः) 2. 3. 15; 6. 7. 42; (9) Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Brahman, Yama and Sthāṇu (Śiva) perform there a सत्र at the end of every thousand aeons (उपासते यत्र सत्रं सहस्रयुगपर्यये) 2. 3. 13; 6. 7. 43, 46.
बिल्वक: Bilvaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who bathes there washes off his sin and goes to heaven (धूतपाप्मा दिवं व्रजेत्) 13. 26. 12; (according to Nī. on Bom. Ed. on 13. 25. 13 all the holy places listed here are situated on the river Godāvarī; for his remark see Gaṅgādvāra).
बृहद्वती: Bṛhadvatī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 29, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
ब्रह्मकुल्या: Brahmakulyā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 34, 13 (for other details see Bṛhadvatī)
ब्रह्मगुहा: Brahmaguhā f.: Name of a place (?) Kṛṣṇa entered the ancient (पौराणी) Brahmaguhā and saw there before him the merging of the earth (in the ocean) (मही-सत्र); he, having thrown the Daityas, ser-pents and the Dānavas into disorder, rescued the earth (स पौराणीं ब्रह्मगुहां प्र-विष्टो महीसत्रं भारताग्रे ददर्श । स चैव गाम् उद्दधाराग्र्यकर्मा विक्षोभ्य दैत्यान् उरगान् दानवांश् च ॥ ) 13. 143. 16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 158. 17: (महीसत्रं पृथिव्याश् छादनं मज्जनम् इति यावत्; Comm. Vādirāja, however, ब्रह्मगुहां वेदहृदयम्).
ब्रह्मण: Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam1 nt.: Name of a sacred place; also known as Brahmodumbara (ब्रह्मोदुम्बरम् इत्य् एव प्रकाशं भुवि भारत) 3. 81. 58. A. Description: Described as best (उत्तम) 3. 81. 58; holy (पुण्य) 5. 187. 24. B. Holiness: At this place there are the कुण्डस् of seven sages and the field (केदार) of Kapiṣṭhala; one who bathes in these two places and, being pure and having a controlled mind (शुचिः प्रयतमानसः), worships god Brahman he is cleansed of all sins and reaches heaven 3. 81. 59-60. C. Epic event: One of the sacred places visited by Ambā where she bathed and practised severe austerities 5. 187. 24-25, 28. [See Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam2, Brahmasthāna].

Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। If a person of a lower birth bathes there he becomes a Brāhmaṇa; and if a Brāhmaṇa bathes there he, with a pure soul, attains (after death) the highest condition (तत्र वर्णावरः स्नात्वा ब्राह्मण्यं लभते नरः । ब्राह्मणश् च विशुद्धात्मा गच्-छेत परमां गतिम् ॥ ) 3. 81. 95. [See Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam1 and Brahmasthāna]
ब्रह्मणः: Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam1 nt.: Name of a sacred place; also known as Brahmodumbara (ब्रह्मोदुम्बरम् इत्य् एव प्रकाशं भुवि भारत) 3. 81. 58. A. Description: Described as best (उत्तम) 3. 81. 58; holy (पुण्य) 5. 187. 24. B. Holiness: At this place there are the कुण्डस् of seven sages and the field (केदार) of Kapiṣṭhala; one who bathes in these two places and, being pure and having a controlled mind (शुचिः प्रयतमानसः), worships god Brahman he is cleansed of all sins and reaches heaven 3. 81. 59-60. C. Epic event: One of the sacred places visited by Ambā where she bathed and practised severe austerities 5. 187. 24-25, 28. [See Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam2, Brahmasthāna].

Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। If a person of a lower birth bathes there he becomes a Brāhmaṇa; and if a Brāhmaṇa bathes there he, with a pure soul, attains (after death) the highest condition (तत्र वर्णावरः स्नात्वा ब्राह्मण्यं लभते नरः । ब्राह्मणश् च विशुद्धात्मा गच्-छेत परमां गतिम् ॥ ) 3. 81. 95. [See Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam1 and Brahmasthāna]
ब्रह्मणस्: Brahmaṇas tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to Brahman; described as best (उत्तम); by worshipping god Brahman there one gets the fruit of a Rājasūya and an Aśvamedha sacrifice 3. 82. 88.
ब्रह्मतुङ्ग: Brahmatuṅga1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting it (समासाद्य) one who is pure and has controlled his mind (शुचिः प्रयतमानसः) and one who is virtuous and is free of the quality of passion (सुकृती विरजाः) wins the world of Brahman 3. 80. 96.
Brahmatuṅga2 m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the north (उदीच्यां दिशि) 7. 57. 23; Arjuna saw it while he was on his way to the place of Śiva to propitiate him to get his Pāśupatāstra 7. 57. 27.
ब्रह्ममेध्या: Brahmamedhyā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 29, 13 (for other details see Bṛhadvatī).
ब्रह्मयोनि: Brahmayoni f.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Holiness: Having reached this तीर्थ and having bathed there one who is pure and has controlled his mind (शुचिः प्रयतमा-नसः) reaches the world of Brahman and purifies his family up to seven generations; there is no doubt about that (पुनात्य् आसप्त-मं चैव कुलं नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः) 3. 81. 121. B. Epic event: Balarāma went there from the Agnitīrtha; he bathed there and gave riches of various kinds; from there he went to the Kauberatīrtha 9. 46. 20, 22. C. Mythological event: Brahmadeva created (the worlds) there; having bathed there with all the gods Brahmadeva, formerly, created according to the rites foods for gods (ससर्ज भगवान् यत्र सर्वलोकपितामहः । तत्रा-प्लुत्य ततो ब्रह्मा सह देवैः प्रभुः पुरा । ससर्ज चान्नानि ततः देवतानां यथाविधि) 9. 46. 21.
ब्रह्मवालुका: Brahmavālukā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated along the river Devikā; by bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) one does not grieve over death (न शोचेन् मरणं ततः) 3. 80. 114.
ब्रह्मशाला: Brahmaśālā f.: Name of a river. Situated in the east 3. 85. 3, near the mountain Mahendra (?) 3. 85. 16; described as holy (पुण्या), famous (ख्याता), and crowded by those who have washed off their sins (धूतपाप्मभिर् आकीर्णा); her very sight is holy (पुण्यं तस्याश् च दर्शनम्) 3. 85. 18.
ब्रह्मसरस्: Brahmasaras nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: In the east 3. 85. 3; in the vicinity of the Gaya mountain, Gayā, Mahānadī and Gayaśiras 3. 85. 7, 8. B. Origin: It was created by god Brahman (सरश् च ब्रह्मनिर्मितम्) 13. 151. 24; 9. 50. 19. C. Description: Holy, very holy (पुण्य) 13. 151. 24, (सुपुण्य) 3. 93. 10; 13. 96. 7; auspicious (शिव) 3. 85. 6; 13. 151 24; removing all sins (सर्वपापहर) 13. 151. 24; best (उत्तम) 3. 93. 10; famous in the three worlds (त्रिलोकविख्यात) 13. 151. 24; liked by sages (ऋषिजुष्ट) 3. 93. 10; resorted to by gods and sages (सेवितं त्रिदशर्षिभिः) 3. 85. 6; a तीर्थ of gods (देवस्य तीर्थे) 13. 96. 7; adorned by the Dharmāraṇya (धर्मारण्योपशोभित) 3. 82. 74; 13. 26. 55. D. Holiness: (1) Mahādeva is always present there 3. 93. 12; (2) Eternal Dharma himself lived there (उवास च स्वयं यत्र धर्मो राजन् सनातनः) 3. 93. 11; (3) If one stays there overnight one becomes pure and gets the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice (पुण्डरीकम् अवाप्नोति प्रभातां शर्वरीं शुचिः) 13. 26. 55; 3. 82. 74; (4) By circumambulating the यूप raised there by Brahman one gets the fruit of a Vājapeya 3. 82. 75. E. Importance: (1) It is the source of all rivers (सर्वासां सरितां चैव समुद्भेदः) 3. 93. 12; (2) The river Sarasvatī, in the by-gone days, arose in this lake; sages know this (प्रसृतासि महाभागे सरसो ब्रह्मणः पुरा । जानन्ति त्वां सरिच्छ्रेष्ठे मुन-यः) 9. 50. 19; (3) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 24, 2. F. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas in their तीर्थ-यात्रा lived there and offered four-monthly sacrifices and a great Ṛṣiyajña (चातुर्मा-स्यैस् तदेजिरे । ऋषियज्ञेन महता) near the Akṣayavaṭa 3. 93. 13. G. Past and mythological events: (1) Brahmadeva raised his यूप there (ब्रह्मणो यूप उच्छ्रितः) 3. 82. 75; (2) Agastya went from there to Vaivasvata (Yama) 3. 93. 11; (3) Śukra, Aṅgiras and other sages reached there in their तीर्थयात्रा; they bathed there and ate lotus stalks and blossoms (विगाह्य ते भुक्तबिसप्रसूनाः); some of them dug out lotus stalks and roots (केचिद् बिसान्य् अखनंस् तत्र राजन्न् अन्ये मृणालान्य् अखनंस् तत्र विप्राः); when the पुष्कर collected by Agastya from the lake disappear-ed he doubted his companions; each one of them then took oath to prove his innocence 13. 96. 8ff; (4) Many Brāhmaṇas used to come there and perform the four-monthly sacrifices according to the ancient rites (चातुर्मास्येनायजन्त आर्षेण विधिना); there the Brāhmaṇas, learned in the Vedas, sitting in the सदस्, narrated holy stories of the high-souled ones 3. 93. 13-15; (5) Gaya, son of Amūrtarayas, performed his famous sacrifice near this lake (अस्य सरसः समीपे); in this sacrifice many दक्षिणास् and large quantities of food were supplied; this and other stories of Gaya Āmūrtarayasa were told by Śamaṭha 3. 93. 16-27.
ब्रह्मस्थान: Brahmasthāna nt.: Name of a sacred place. By staying there for three nights one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows and goes to heaven 3. 83. 32 [See Brahmaṇaḥ sthānam1, 2]
ब्रह्माणी: Brahmāṇī f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 32, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
ब्रह्मावर्त: Brahmāvarta m.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there one goes to the world of Brahman 3. 81. 43; one who observes chastity and has a composed mind (ब्रह्मचारी समा-हितः), if he visits Brahmāvarta he obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha and goes to heaven 3. 82. 38.
ब्राह्मणी: Brāhmaṇī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who practises chastity and has con-trolled his sense organs, if he visits this तीर्थ he goes to the world of Brahman in a con-veyance which has the colour of a lotus (पद्मवर्णेन यानेन) 3. 82. 52.
बदरी: Badarī f., Badaryāśrama m.: Name of a tree and also of an आश्रम situated near it (तम् आश्रमपदं … बदरी नाम विश्रुतम् 3. 45. 19); once referred to as Badarāśrama (12. 326. 99). A. Location: In the north (अस्यां दीशि … उत्तरायाम्) 5. 109. 3; on the Gandha-mādana mountain (गन्धमादनम् आसाद्य बदर्यां च) 1. 32. 3; प्रवेक्षामो … पर्वतं गन्धमादनम् ॥ विशाला बदरी यत्र) 3. 142. 22-23; 3. 145. 2, 10; 12. 321. 13; 12. 330. 41; 12. 331. 22. B. Descrip-tion: Holy (आश्रमपदं पुण्य्म्) 3. 45. 19; (पुण्या) 3. 88. 22; auspicious (शुभा) 3. 145. 18; heavenly (दिव्या) 3. 145. 19; pleasing (रम्या) 12. 126. 3; (मनोरमा) 3. 145. 17; resplendent (स्निग्धा) 3. 145. 17; very glorious (श्रिया परमया युताम्) 3. 145. 17; very lustrous (अतिद्युतिसमन्विता) 3. 145. 18; extensive (विस्तीर्णा) 3. 145. 18 (see विशाला as its characteristic in the next section); resorted to by great sages (मह-र्षिगणसेविता) 3. 145. 19; having a round trunk (वृत्तस्कन्धा) 3. 145. 17; having extensive branches (विशालशाखा) 3. 145. 18; offering dense shade (अविरलच्छाया) 3. 145. 17; full of shining, and densely grown soft leaves (पत्रैः स्निग्धैर् अविर-लैर् उपेताम् मृदुभिः) 3. 145. 18; always full of heavenly and densely growing fruit which are tasty and have sweet juice (फलैर् उपचितैर् दिव्यैर् आचितां स्वादुभिर् भृशम् । मधुस्रवैः सदा) 3. 145. 19; resorted to always by hosts of different kinds of birds delighted due to excitement (मदप्रमुदितैर् नित्यं नानाद्विजगणैर् युताम्) 3. 145. 19; it grew on a region which was free from biting insects, which was rich in roots, fruits and water, covered with green grass, visited by gods and Gandharvas, on the ground which was naturally level, auspicious, soft to touch due to snow, and free from thorns (अदं-शमशके देशे बहुमूलफलोदके । नील-शाद्वलसंछन्ने देवगन्धर्वसेविते ॥ सुसमीकृतभूभागे स्वभावविहिते शुभे । जातां हिममृदुस्पर्शे देशेऽपहतकण्टके) 3. 145. 20-21. C. Characteristics: (1) Extensive, wide growing, hence often referr-ed to as विशाला Badarī 3. 13. 12.; 3. 88. 22-23; 3. 142. 23; 3. 145. 10; 3. 152. 1; 3. 174. 8; 3. 185. 4; 12. 331. 22 (also cf. विस्तीर्णा in section B above); (2) Characterized by the आश्रम of the sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa 3. 45. 18-20; 3. 88. 22; 3. 142. 23; 3. 145. 16; (Nārāyaṇasthāna) 3. 174. 9; 5. 109. 4: 13. 153. 42; (3) Gaṅgā originated at Badarī (यतः प्रववृते गङ्गा) 3. 45. 20; Gaṅgā flew near it (गङ्गा … विशालां बदरीम् अनु) 3. 88. 23; (4) Sages and gods always visit it to bow down to god Nārāyaṇa (ऋषयो यत्र देवाश् च … प्राप्य नित्यं नमस्यन्ति देवं नारायोणं वि-भुम्) 3. 88. 24; (5) It cannot be seen by gods or by high-souled sages (यन् न शक्यं सुरैर् द्रष्टुं ऋषिभिर् वा महात्मभिः । तद् आश्रमपदं पुण्यं बदरी नाम वि-श्रुतम् ॥ ) 3. 45. 19; (6) One could see the lotus pond loved by Kubera from Badarī (कुबेरकान्तां नलिनीम्) 3. 174. 9-10. D. Epic events: (1) Ghaṭotkaca and his Rākṣasas carried the Pāṇḍavas, Draupadī and the Brāhmaṇas to Badarī 3. 145. 10, 22; (2) Bhīma told the Rākṣasas, guard-ing the lotus lake of Kubera, that he with his brothers had reached Badarī from where he went out in search of the lotus having heavenly fragrance 3. 152. 1; (3) On their return journey from Gandha-mādana, the Pāṇḍavas reached Badari and lived there for a month 3. 174. 8, 11; (4) Dhṛtarāṣṭra while praising Kṛṣṇa said that he knew him as the greatest sage who had lived with Nara at Badarī for a very long time (नरेण सहितं देवं बदर्यां सुचि-रोषितम्) 13. 153. 42. E. Past events: (1) As advised by the supreme god Hari Nārā-yaṇa, Nārada once hastened to Badarāśrama from Śvetadvīpa to see there Nara and Nārā-yaṇa (नारदः । नरनारायणौ द्रष्टुं प्राद्रवत् बदराश्रमम्) 12. 326. 99; he hastened to Badarī hermitage (बदरीम् आश्रमं यत् तु नारदः प्राद्रवत् पुनः । नरनारायणौ द्रष्टुम्) 12. 331. 15-16; Nārada dropped down to Gandhamādana from the peak of the great mountain Meru in order to reach Badaryāśrama (महा-मेरोर् गिरेः शृङ्गात् प्रच्युतो गन्धमाद-नम् । नारदः … तं देशम् अगमद् राजन् बदर्याश्रमम्) 12. 321. 13-14; (निपपात च खात् तूर्णम् विशालां बदरीम् अनु) 12. 331. 22-23; (2) A brahmanical sage (विप्रर्षि) told king Sumitra that in the bygone days, while he was once on a pil-grimage (तीर्थान्य् अनुचरन्), he reached Naranārāyaṇāśrama near Badarī 12. 126. 2-3; (3) At Badarī, Manu, with raised hands, standing on one foot, head bent downwards and with unblinking eyes, pra-ctised severe austerities for ten thousand years (ऊर्ध्वबाहुर् विशालायां बदर्याम् स … । एकपादस्थितस् तीव्रं चचार सुम-हत् तपः ॥ अवाक्शिरास् तथा चापि नेत्रैर् अनिमिषैर् दृढम्) 3. 185. 4-5; (4) Ser-pent Śeṣa was disgusted with the behavi-our of his brother-serpents; hence, among other holy places, he repaired to Badarī to practise austerities 1. 32. 3; (5) In the Kṛta age a Rākṣasa named Cārvāka practised austerities for many years at Badarī 12. 39. 39; (6) In the Kṛta age Nara and Nārāyaṇa went to Badaryāśrama in a golden cart to practise austerities (बदर्याश्रमम् आसाद्य शकटे कनका-मये) 12. 321. 10; there they practised austerities for several myriad years (वर्षा-युतान् बहून्) 3. 41. 1; 12. 330. 41; (7) Kṛṣṇa practised austerities with raised hands and standing on one foot, living only on wind, at Viśālā Badarī for hundred years 3. 13. 12; (8) After destroying the sacrifice of Dakṣa, the शूल of Rudra rushed with great force to Badaryāśrama (सहसा-गच्छद् बदर्याश्रमम् अन्तिकात्) and fell with great vehemence on the chest of Nārā-yaṇa 12. 330. 44. [See Naranārāyaṇāśrama; for Badarikā tīrtha see Vol. 1. 393]
ब्रह्माश्रमपद: Brahmāśramapada nt.: The place where the Brahmāśrama stood. A. Location: On the slope of Hima-vant (हिमवतः पार्श्वे) 13. 10. 5. B. Des-cription: Holy (पुण्य) 13. 10. 6; pleasing (रम्य) 13. 10. 7; surrounded by flowering forests (पुष्पितकानन) 13. 10. 7; full of many clusters of different kinds of trees (नानावृक्षगणायुत) 13. 10. 6; full of many shrubs and creepers (बहुगुल्मलता-कीर्ण) 13. 10. 6; resorted to by deer and birds (मृगद्विजनिषेवित) 13. 10. 6; full of sounds of Siddhas and Cāraṇas (सिद्ध-चारणसंघुष्ट) 13. 10. 7: full of many ascetics observing vows, adorned by ascetics, thronged by brahmanical ascetics observ-ing regulations and vows, full of those who were initiated, who took limited food, and who had disciplined themselves, resorted to by Vālakhilyas and many mendicants (व्रतिभिर् बहुभिः कीऋणं तापसैर् उपशो-भितम् ॥ ब्राह्मणैश् च … नियमव्रतसं-पन्नैः समाकीर्णं तपस्विभिः । दीक्षितैर्  … यताहारैः कृतात्मभिः ॥ … वालखिल्यैश् च बहुभिर् यतिभिश् च निषेवितम्) 13. 10. 7-9; resounding with the sounds of Vedic recitations (वेदाध्ययनघोषैश् च नादि-तम्) 13. 10. 9. C. Organisation: A कुल-पति presided over it and decided whether a newcomer was to be permitted in the आश्रम 13. 10. 12-15 (see the next section). D. Past events: A certain Śūdra once arrived at Brahmāśrama and was honour-ed by the ascetics; he desired to practise धर्म (इच्छामि धर्मं चर्तुम्) 13. 10. 13, and hence requested the head of the आश्रम (कुलपति) to teach him and initiate him into the ascetic practices (तन् मां त्वं भगवन् वक्तुं प्रव्राजयितुम् अर्हसि) 13. 10. 13 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 10. 14: प्रव्राज-यितुम् विधिवत् स्वोचितं कर्म त्याजयितुम्); the head of the आश्रम told him that it was not possible for him to be an ascetic (प्र-व्राजक) and live in the आश्रम (न शक्यम् इह शूद्रेण लिङ्गम् आश्रित्य वर्तितुम्) 13. 10. 15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 10. 16: लिङ्गं संन्यासचिह्नम्); so the Śūdra went some distance from the आश्रमपद and constru-cted a cottage for himself; he put up an altar, levelled the ground, and raised abodes for gods (गत्वाश्रमपदाद् दूरम् उटजं कृतवांस् तु सः । तत्र वेदिं च भूमिं च देवतायतनानि च । निवेश्य॑) 13. 10. 17 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 13. 10. 20: वेदीं पूजार्थं, भूमिं शयनाद्यर्थम्); a certain ascetic (मुनि, ऋषि, तापस) who acted as a priest for the rites of manes (पितृकार्य) of this Śūdra became in his next birth the Purohita of the king (viz. the Śūdra who was born as a king); when the Purohita was told by the king about his past life he went to the same Brahmāśrama to practise austerities; he obtained great perfection (सिद्धिं परां प्राप्तः) and was respected by the residents of the आश्रम 13. 10. 10-59.
बर्बर: Barbara m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (किराता बर्-बराः) 6. 10. 55; natives of Uttarāpatha (उत्तरापथजन्मानः … किराता बर्बरैः सह) 12. 200. 40; Nakula conquered them when he went to the west of Indra-prastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रती-चीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; (वासुदेव-जिताम् आशाम्) 2. 29. 1; 2. 23. 10; they lived by the gulf of the (western) ocean (सागर-कुक्षिस्थान्) 2. 29. 15; (सागरानूपगान्) 3. 48. 19. B. Origin: Barbaras and others were created by Nandinī, the cow of Vasiṣṭha, from her foam (बर्बरांस् तथा … फेनतः सा ससर्ज ह) 1. 165. 36. C. Low social status: Barbaras counted among those who were reduced to the status of वृषल due to their non-respecting Brāhmaṇas 13. 35. 17-18; they were classed as Dasyus 12. 65. 15 or म्लेच्छस् 1. 165. 36; 12. 65. 14; they did not believe in Bhūtapati being the अध्यक्ष of all beings; they were sinful and roamed over the earth living the way dogs, crows, बलस् (?) and vultures lived; they did not exist in the Kṛtayuga and were to be found since the Tretāyuga 12. 200. 38, 40-42; they lived in countries but led the life of Dasyus; king Māndhātṛ asked Indra what was the duty of people like Barbaras and how they should be controlled; thereupon Indra told him what the duties of Dasyus were 12. 65. 13, 15, 17-22 (for citations see Kirāta). D. Epic events: (1) Nakula subjugated Barbaras and their kings (बर्-बरांश् चैव तान् सर्वान् अनयद् वशम् । … वशे कृत्वा च पार्थिवान्) and collected jewels as tribute for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 29. 15-16; the kings attended the Rāja-sūya and acted as servers (यज्ञे … परि-वेषकान्) 3. 48. 22; (2) On the fourteenth day of war Barbaras, holding different kinds of weapons (विविधायुधपाणयः) faced Sātyaki 7. 95. 13; he killed them and many others by thousands (काम्बोजानां सह-स्रैस् तु … बर्बराणां तथैव च) 7. 95. 38.
बलिराष्ट्र: Balirāṣṭra nt. (sg.): Name of a Jana-papa. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (बलिराष्ट्रं च केवलम्) 6. 10. 43.
बलिह: Baliha m. (pl.): Name of a people. Listed by Bhīma among the eighteen peoples whose kings were known to have extirpated their kinsmen, friends and rela-tives; Arkaja was then the king of Balīhas (अष्टादशेमे राजानः प्रख्याता … । ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्ध-वान् ॥ … अर्कजश् च बलीहानाम्) 5. 72. 11, 14.
बहिर्गिर्य: Bahirgirya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (बहिर्गिर्याङ्गमलदा … ) 6. 10. 48 [cf. Antargirya].
बहुवाद्य: Bahuvādya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (बहुवाद्याश् च) 6. 10. 53.
बोध: Bodha m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5, (बोधा मोकास् तथैव च) 6. 10. 38. B. Epic event: Bodhas mentioned among those peoples who due to fear of Jarāsandha migrated to the west (प्रतीचीं दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ शूर-सेना भद्रकारा बोधाः) 2. 13. 24-25.
